key_insight: THz time-domain spectroscopy can non-destructively fingerprint specific grain-boundary defects in organic halide perovskite films by linking terahertz absorption features to defect species and concentration.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical, room-temperature quality-control tool for defect diagnosis and passivation in perovskite solar-cell manufacturing.
method: Measure 0.3–3.0 THz spectra of sequential-vacuum-evaporated perovskite thin films.
Identify intrinsic phonons and grain-boundary-localized defect vibrational fingerprints across MAPbI3, MAPbBr3, FAPbI3, and CsPbI3.
Use oscillator-strength analysis and a THz reference library for quantitative, species-specific defect mapping.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the 1.58 THz absorption in MAPbI3 scales linearly with XPS-quantified CH3NH2 defect concentration, supporting THz-TDS as a direct defect meter.
watch_item: The approach depends on building a robust material-specific THz fingerprint library and may be sensitive to film composition, fabrication route, and spectral overlap between modes.
paper_title: Terahertz Time-Domain Spectroscopy as a Universal Defect Fingerprinting Tool for Organic Halide Perovskite Solar Cells
